tasks.short: Hear the delay or descent news from the cockpit, compose the announcement in the needed languages, announce delays and descent preparations, and answer follow-up questions.

steps.what: Flight attendant hears the delay or descent information from the cockpit by interphone
Flight attendant composes the delay announcement in each needed language
Flight attendant checks the filled-in announcement against the cockpit's information: reason, new time and each language version say the same
Flight attendant announces flight delays over the public address system
Flight attendant answers passengers' follow-up questions about connections

tasks.design: The crew tablet ({OPS_SYSTEM}) holds delay announcement templates in the operator's languages, approved by cabin safety; the attendant fills in the reason and new time, checks the text against what the cockpit said and reads it out. On aircraft with cabin screens a recorded descent announcement plays. Hearing the news from the cockpit, announcing delays and answering follow-up questions stay with the attendant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each delay announcement was composed on the spot, often in two or three languages.
tasks.enabler_now: Crew tablets hold approved announcement templates; cabin systems play recordings.
tasks.still_hard: Delay reasons change while the announcement is being made.
tasks.human_edge: Reading the cabin's mood and choosing the right tone.

reach.learn: Whether templates make delay messages more consistent.

evidence.claim: Crew tablets can hold approved announcement texts, and cabin systems can play recorded announcements.

assumptions: Boundary: from the cockpit's information to questions answered; rebooking passengers is outside.
Input contract: delay reasons and times from the cockpit; templates kept by cabin safety; fallback is composing on the spot.

Announcing delays live and the check keep their full time. s2 keeps 50 because the approved phrases in each language replace composing on the spot while the attendant fills in reason and time; s4 keeps 70 because about a fifth of flights have screens with a recorded descent announcement.
research_questions: Do passengers ask fewer questions after a template announcement?

incremental.description: Flight attendant reports missing template phrases to cabin safety.

approvals.approved_version: The delay announcement text with reason and new time exactly as checked by the attendant in s2c, read out once over the public address system; any change from the cockpit needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most routes need one language and few aircraft have screens, so s2 keeps 75 and s4 keeps 90 (5.5); high: multilingual routes and the fleet mix as assumed (14.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read boarding passes at the door, greet passengers and direct them to their assigned seats, and count passengers against the boarded number.

steps.what: Flight attendant reads boarding passes at the aircraft door
Flight attendant greets passengers boarding aircraft and directs them to assigned seats
Flight attendant counts passengers twice and compares with the boarded number from the gate

tasks.design: Departure control ({OPS_SYSTEM}) sends the boarded count and seat map to the crew tablet, so the attendant counts once and the tablet shows any difference, instead of counting twice and phoning the gate. Greeting passengers and directing them to seats stay with the attendant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Passengers were counted twice by hand and the number checked with the gate by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Departure control systems can send boarded counts and seat maps to crew devices.
tasks.still_hard: A wrong count still holds the door until it is resolved.
tasks.human_edge: A warm welcome that sets the tone for the flight.

reach.learn: Whether count differences are resolved faster.

evidence.claim: Departure control systems can send boarded counts and seat maps to crew devices.

assumptions: Boundary: from passengers at the door to the passenger count; closing the door is outside.
Input contract: boarded count from departure control; fallback is counting twice and phoning the gate.
Greeting and directing do not change.
research_questions: Do count differences delay departure less often?

incremental.description: Flight attendant reports tablet count errors to the gate.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the tablet count often differs from the cabin, so many flights still need a second count and a call to the gate and s3 keeps 75 (4.5); high: counts match on most flights and s3 keeps 50 (9.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hear passengers' questions, look up arrival times and connecting gates, answer questions about the flight, weather, routes and schedules, and explain services and the aircraft.

steps.what: Passenger asks a question about the flight or connections
Flight attendant looks up arrival times and connecting gates or asks the cockpit
Flight attendant answers passengers' questions about flights, weather, travel routes, arrival times and schedules
Flight attendant explains on-board services and the aircraft

tasks.design: The airline app and seatback screens show live arrival time, weather at the destination and connecting gates from the flight data ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so many passengers find answers without asking. The crew tablet shows the same data, so the attendant does not phone the cockpit for times and gates. Explaining services and answering what the screens do not cover stay with the attendant; nothing is generated, all answers quote live flight data.
tasks.previous_blocker: Times and gates were known only in the cockpit and passed on by interphone.
tasks.enabler_now: Airline apps and cabin screens show live flight data in flight.
tasks.still_hard: Anxious passengers ask in person even when the screen shows the answer.
tasks.human_edge: Reassuring a nervous flyer about turbulence.
tasks.altitude: The attendant answers what screens do not cover.

reach.learn: Whether passengers check the app before asking.

evidence.claim: Airline apps and cabin screens can show live arrival times and connecting gates during flight.
Air carriers fall under NIS2 Annex I, so in-flight data links fall within the carrier's security duties.

assumptions: Boundary: from the passenger's question to the answer; rebooking is outside.
Input contract: arrival times and gates from flight operations; destination weather from the operator's feed; fallback is asking the cockpit.
Passengers who read the app instead of asking spend about the same time; priced as customer time.
research_questions: Do questions about arrival times fall?

incremental.description: Flight attendant corrects passengers misreading the screens.
Passengers look up times and gates in the app or on the screen.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older aircraft have no screens or connection and anxious passengers ask anyway, so s2 keeps 70 and s3 keeps 90 (12.8); high: connected aircraft where many passengers read the screens (29.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take meal and drink orders and collect cash and card payments.

steps.what: Passenger chooses and pays for meals and beverages
Flight attendant takes the order and rings it up on the handheld
Flight attendant collects money for meals and beverages in cash or by card

tasks.design: Passengers pre-order and pay for meals in the airline app before the flight, and on board the handheld point of sale ({OTHER}) takes contactless cards offline and settles them after landing, so less cash is handled. Serving and taking cash from the few who still pay cash stay with the attendant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most sales were cash, taken and noted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Handheld tills take contactless cards offline; airline apps take meal pre-orders.
tasks.still_hard: Card payments taken offline can fail when settled after landing.
tasks.human_edge: Handling a passenger whose card is declined without embarrassment.

evidence.claim: Handheld tills on aircraft can take contactless cards offline and settle them after landing.

assumptions: Boundary: from the passenger's order to payment collected; counting cash and catering stock are outside.
Input contract: menu and prices loaded on the handheld by catering; pre-orders from the app; fallback is cash.
Passengers who pre-order or tap a card spend about the same time as paying cash; priced as customer time.
Each card payment is the passenger's own tap on the amount shown on the handheld; settling the flight's card payments after landing belongs to closing the sales, which is outside this task.
research_questions: Do cash differences after flights fall?

incremental.description: Flight attendant handles declined offline card payments.
Passengers pre-order in the app or tap a card.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many passengers pay cash and few pre-order, so s2 and s3 keep 85 (14.0); high: most pay by card or pre-order as designed (29.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The flight attendant keeps announcing, welcoming, reassuring and serving passengers; composing announcements, counting twice, looking up times and counting cash shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the crew tablet for flight data
role.ambitious_version: An attendant who spends saved time with passengers who need help.
